name: Fernhook Falls
reason: Rule 1: DBCA Explore Parks has its own visitor page (exploreparks.dbca.wa.gov.au/site/fernhook-falls, opened). Rule 2: Deep River cascades over granite into Rowell's Pool, with walk trails and wheelchair-accessible boardwalks; DBCA says 'spend a few hours, or a few days'; free, open access. Rule 3: a distinct waterfall site in Mount Frankland South National Park (a different park from Mount Frankland NP). Rule 4: permanent (flow varies by season: a torrent in winter, a trickle in summer).
objection: Only one counted source and no Wikipedia article; in summer the falls are a trickle, so the draw is seasonal and it sits on a remote forest road. Also has a campground on site: keep the falls as the place, not the campground.

name: Mandalay Beach
reason: Rule 1: DBCA visitor page in D'Entrecasteaux NP (opened) calls it 'one of the most beautiful beaches in the Walpole area' and 'a great stop between Manjimup and Walpole'. Rule 2: boardwalks to the beach, whale-watching platforms on the limestone cliffs, interpretive information on the 1911 wreck of the barque Mandalay (visible at low tide), fishing; open access (park entry fee). Rule 3: distinct beach; the wreck is part of this spot, not a separate one. Rule 4: permanent. Second-tier beach a real source names: keep.
objection: One counted source and no Wikipedia article; the wreck is only visible at low tide, and it is a gravel-road detour off the South Western Highway.

name: Mount Frankland National Park
reason: Rule 1: DBCA park page (opened) promotes the Mount Frankland Wilderness Lookout over the Walpole Wilderness, bushwalks of several lengths, picnic area at Towerman's Hut. Rule 2: summit climb/lookout and walks easily fill an hour or more; free, open access. Rule 3: distinct park (granite peak over 31,000 ha of tingle, jarrah and karri). Rule 4: permanent.
objection: One counted source and modest views (679/yr); the draw is really the Wilderness Lookout and summit walk, so if the run also has 'Mount Frankland Wilderness Lookout' or 'Mount Frankland summit' as a candidate, keep only one (the park, pinned at the lookout car park) as a duplicate. Small park: per COVERAGE it is a standalone spot, not a destination.

name: Peppermint Grove Beach
reason: Rule 1: the regional tourism board Visit Bunbury Geographe (visitbunburygeographe.com.au/explore-the-region/capel/, opened) names it 'one of the region's best beaches' and a Capel-region must-do (swim, canoe the Capel River mouth, fishing areas, sunset); the candidate had no counted source, and this is one. Rule 2: swimming beach with beach park, lookout (about 120 steps, 360-degree view), BBQs; open access. Rule 3: distinct beach. Rule 4: permanent. Second-tier beach a real source names: keep.
objection: One counted source; it is a small holiday settlement's local beach on a 29 km stretch of similar Geographe Bay coast, and most of the board's copy promotes the holiday park beside it. A friend flying in would go only if staying nearby: arguable, but the rule keeps beaches a board names.
